people: Tan Sri Mohamed Azman Yahya (Independent Non-executive Director, AIA Group Limited, 24 February 2014 to 28 May 2020; member of Bank Negara Malaysia's Board of Directors from 1 June 2020)
summary: Bank Negara Malaysia's own board page lists Tan Sri Mohamed Azman Yahya as an Independent Non-Executive Member of its Board of Directors, appointed on 1 June 2020, chairing the Board Governance Committee and sitting on the Board Risk Committee. Among his past positions the page lists board membership of AIA Group Limited. The central bank's page names the company but does not say what kind of business it is. AIA Group Limited's own stock-exchange announcement states that his appointment as an Independent Non-executive Director, and as a member of the Remuneration Committee and Nomination Committee, took effect from 24 February 2014 for a term of three years. A further AIA Group announcement dated 28 May 2020 states that Mr Yahya 'will retire upon conclusion of the AGM' as an Independent Non-executive Director and leaves the Nomination and Remuneration Committees. AIA Group Limited's 2019 annual report describes the group as 'the largest independent publicly listed pan-Asian life insurance group' and says AIA Group Limited is listed on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited under stock code 1299 - so the insurer is described by its own filings as independent and publicly listed, that is, private-sector rather than state-owned. Bank Negara Malaysia is the public side. The gap between leaving the insurer's board and joining the central bank's board is four days.
move: left the board of AIA Group Limited, a publicly listed pan-Asian life insurance group, and joined Bank Negara Malaysia's board four days later

people: Sahar A. Al-Rumaih (Deputy Governor and Member of the Board of Directors, Central Bank of Kuwait, since September 2022)
summary: The Central Bank of Kuwait's own profile page for its Deputy Governor states that Sahar A. Al-Rumaih has been Deputy Governor and a member of the Board of Directors since September 2022, and that almost her whole earlier career was spent in commercial banking. The page says she began in corporate banking and credit at two Kuwaiti banks, then in 2000 joined what it calls 'a large commercial bank in Kuwait', where she was General Manager of the Corporate Credit Division from 2011 to 2018, Head of the Retail Banking Division from 2015 to 2018, and Deputy Chief Executive Officer heading the Corporate and International Banking Divisions from 2018 to 2021. In 2021 she moved to what the page calls 'another major bank headquartered in Kuwait' as Deputy CEO for the Corporate Banking Division. From February 2022 until her appointment as Deputy Governor she was Chairperson of a local capital investment company that the page says is regulated by the Capital Markets Authority. The central bank does not name any of these employers, and names the type only in the one case: the 2000 employer is called a commercial bank. It does not characterise the second bank, nor call the investment company an asset manager or brokerage. The private side of the career is therefore the commercial-banking employment from 2000 to 2021; the public side is the Central Bank of Kuwait. Because the bank gives the career but withholds the employers' names, no firms are listed.
move: two decades in commercial banking in Kuwait, rising to Deputy CEO, then into the central bank as Deputy Governor

central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
people: 陳思寬 (Chen Szu-kuan), Director of the 21st Board of Directors of the Central Bank of the Republic of China, term 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030, while serving as Chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited and Chairman of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited
summary: The Central Bank of the Republic of China publishes the curriculum-vitae table for its 21st Board of Directors, appointed for a term running from 27 January 2025 to 26 January 2030. In that official table the director 陳思寬 (Chen Szu-kuan) is listed with her current occupation given as Chairman of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited, Chairman of SinoPac Securities Investment Trust Company Limited, and adjunct professor at National Taiwan University. This is not a move but a seat held at the same time as the private role: she sits on the central bank's board while chairing a financial holding company and a securities investment trust firm. The central bank's table names the companies and gives her titles but says nothing about ownership, so it does not itself establish that the SinoPac group is private. The trade publication Caproasia, in an article dated 31 March 2026 on a merger of two SinoPac subsidiaries, describes the planned combined bank of Bank SinoPac and King's Town Bank as 'the 5th largest privately-owned bank in Taiwan' and says SinoPac Financial Holdings was founded in 2002 by the Ho family as part of the Yuen Foong Yu Group. Bank SinoPac's own corporate profile confirms it is a wholly owned subsidiary of SinoPac Financial Holdings Company Limited, formed in 2002 through a share swap with Bank SinoPac and SinoPac Securities, but that profile does not state ownership type. So the private characterisation rests on the trade publication, not on the central bank or the group's own page. The central bank side is public.
status: concurrent private and central bank role, no finding

move: sits on the central bank's board while chairing SinoPac Financial Holdings and SinoPac Securities Investment Trust
